cases.notes: MeadowMart BFF's account/cart preferences endpoint (CC-LAB-0070/CC-LAB-0077); unguarded_deep_merge writes every key of the request body onto the live preferences object with no guard, so a '__proto__'-shaped body pollutes Object.prototype itself (LABGEN-PP-0001). Served at the app's real, canonical URL (see fuzzlab.labgen.emitters.node_express's _REAL_PAGE_CANONICAL). The finding is invisible in this request's own HTTP response by nature -- see tests/test_labgen_prototype_pollution.py's real, executed Node-subprocess proof, and tests/test_labgen_node_bff_app.py for the same route proven reachable inside the fully assembled app over real HTTP.

The secure twin of MMART-0001 (LABGEN-PP-0002): proto_key_filtered_merge skips '__proto__'/'constructor'/'prototype' keys before the merge's own assignment, so the same adversarial body leaves Object.prototype untouched. Served at a deterministic twin URL (CC-LAB-0077's _twin_url_for) since both twins must coexist as distinct live routes in the one assembled app.

MeadowMart BFF's search/highlight endpoint (CC-LAB-0076/CC-LAB-0077); the search term is interpolated directly into `new RegExp(term, 'gi')` with no escaping, so a pathological pattern (e.g. '(a+)+$') causes catastrophic backtracking against the endpoint's own content (LABGEN-RD-0001). Served at the app's real, canonical URL. A real, directly observable real-HTTP timing differential -- see tests/test_labgen_redos.py's in-process proof and tests/test_labgen_node_bff_app.py's real-HTTP proof against the fully assembled app.

The secure twin of MMART-0003 (LABGEN-RD-0002): regex_escape_construct escapes every regex metacharacter in the term before the RegExp is built, so the same adversarial pattern can only ever match itself literally. Served at a deterministic twin URL, same rationale as MMART-0002.
